intelligence.essence: We're not building four apps. We're building ONE ultimate app that morphs — same heart, different identity. One thing to perfect, then it puts on faces.
intelligence.human_view: Shawn's teaching: 'You're just making one ultimate app — full featured — that can morph into different functions or titles or identities.' The mental shift that kills the complexity: stop thinking 'the business app and the space app and the membership app.' There is one app. It walks through different doors — Personal, Business, Space, Membership — and takes the shape of whichever room it's in. Four apps means four builds, four codebases, four drifts, four ways to be 80% done. One app means one thing to perfect, one thing to test, one thing to make utterly awesome. Then it morphs. Build Personal first, complete; then the same bones wear the Business label, the Space label, the Membership label with the login as its front door.
intelligence.simple_view: One app, many faces. Perfect the one thing, then let it put on whichever face the moment needs — Personal, Business, Space, Membership. Never four separate builds.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, it's like one good house with four doors. You don't build four houses — you build one beautiful house, and each door opens into the room you need. Same heart, different room.
intelligence.naya_view: This is the One-App doctrine in its sharpest form (SN-0874's lock, restated by Shawn 2026-11-05 ~01:31Z): my build target is never 'an app' — it is the one morphing master. Personal is the master I finish first; every other door is a label and a lens on the same bones, all synced.
intelligence.ai_view: Architecture constraint: single application core with door-scoped presentation/identity layers (personal|business|space|membership). Forbidden: per-door codebases or divergent feature sets. Build order: master (personal) to complete, then clone-by-label. Sync invariant: a change in one door is true in all doors.
